theme.appSubtitle: Energy‑aware planning for women navigating menopause.

cycle._note_for_devs: No menstrual phases. Instead, an energy/symptom model drives all recommendations. The user logs their energy state daily, plus optional symptoms (hot flashes, sleep quality, joint pain, mood). The app does NOT track cycle days or predict a period.

high.label: High Energy
high.desc: Clear head, good stamina. Your body is ready for more today. Push a bit harder — this window is worth using.
needs: Social plans if you have energy

moderate.label: Moderate Energy
moderate.desc: Steady state. Move well, eat well, sleep on time. This is your sustainable baseline — it's good.

low.label: Rest & Restore
low.desc: Rest is the workout today. Gentle movement, extra water, and permission to go slow. This is hormonal — it will pass.
needs: Gentle yoga or a short walk only
Extra sleep and no guilt about it

energyModel.checkInPrompt: How does your body feel today?

hormoneModel.note: The natural hormone cycle curve is not shown because the menstrual phase model does not apply. Planning is based on your energy check-in and symptom log instead.

low.note: Swap full sessions for stretching, walking, or restorative work. Honor the low-energy day.

moderate.note: Good window for a solid, steady session — nothing you need to push through.

high.note: Your best-energy day. Push your hardest session here.

low.note: Keep it light — review, admin, or rest your mind along with your body.

moderate.note: Steady, sustainable focus — a good day for regular practice or moderate learning.

high.note: Sharpest thinking of the cycle. Tackle the hardest, most complex work today.

hotTub.label: ♨️ Hot Tub / Warm Bath
hotTub.note: Heat therapy can ease joint pain and improve sleep onset — especially valuable in perimenopause.

PM.name: Weight training — compound lifts (prioritize bone density)
Dance class or movement you love
Evening swim or hot tub soak

AM.name: Yin yoga — long holds, no effort
Short walk outside — 15 min is enough

PM.name: Hot bath or hot tub — full recovery

cycleFocusOptions.label: 💪 Build & Maintain Muscle
cycleFocusOptions.note: Resistance training 3-4x/week. Prioritize compound movements. Bone density is the goal, not just aesthetics.

cycleFocusOptions.label: 🧘 Mobility & Joint Health
cycleFocusOptions.note: Yoga and Pilates-forward. Shorter strength sessions. Hot tub and stretching built into every week.

cycleFocusOptions.label: ❤️ Heart Health & Endurance
cycleFocusOptions.note: Zone 2 cardio is your friend — walks, light cycling, swimming. Mix in 1-2 strength sessions.

cycleFocusOptions.label: 🔥 Body Composition
cycleFocusOptions.note: Resistance training takes priority over cardio for menopausal body composition. Protein is your lever.

activity._note: For menopausal users, resistance training to protect bone density is more critical than cardio. Recommend noting this in the activity module.

food.intro: Hormonal changes shift how your body uses food. Protein, phytoestrogens, and anti-inflammatory foods matter more now.

high.headline: Fuel performance — protein first
eat: High-quality protein with every meal (30g+ targets)
limit: Alcohol — disrupts sleep and hot flashes
high.note: On high-energy days your body responds well to training and nutrition. Use this window to eat well and recover properly.

moderate.headline: Steady, balanced & anti-inflammatory
eat: Fiber-rich foods — gut health matters more in menopause
Calcium-rich foods (dairy, fortified alternatives, leafy greens)
moderate.note: Estrogen supports bone health — with less of it, calcium and vitamin D intake becomes critical. Don't undereat.

low.headline: Easy, warm & soothing
eat: Magnesium-rich foods (dark chocolate, pumpkin seeds, leafy greens)
Tryptophan foods for sleep support (turkey, eggs, seeds)
Warm, easy-to-digest meals — soups and stews
low.note: On low-energy days, your nervous system needs calming food, not stimulation. Prioritize warmth, magnesium, and early sleep.

fasting._note: Menopausal women should be more cautious with extended fasting. Muscle loss risk increases without adequate protein. Recommend max 16:8 and only on moderate/high energy days.

high.reason: High energy days tolerate fasting better. Keep protein high when you break the fast.

moderate.reason: A 14-hour overnight fast supports insulin sensitivity without stressing cortisol.

low.reason: On low-energy days, fasting can worsen fatigue and cortisol. Prioritize nourishment.

milestones.label: Glycogen depleting
milestones.bio: Your body is burning through stored glucose. Hunger is normal — it's just your ghrelin pattern.

milestones.label: Ketone shift begins
milestones.bio: Insulin is dropping. Your body is starting to shift toward fat oxidation.

milestones.label: Overnight reset
milestones.bio: A gentle overnight fast is complete. This is a great stopping point for menopausal women.

milestones.label: Ideal window
milestones.bio: 14 hours is a sweet spot — metabolic benefits without muscle-loss risk.

milestones.label: Extended — be mindful
milestones.bio: Extended fasting on top of hormonal changes can stress cortisol. Break with protein first.

sexualHealth.note: Perimenopause does not mean infertility until 12 months after your last period. Contraception may still be relevant. Consult your provider.
sexualHealth.HRTNote: If you are on hormone replacement therapy (HRT), the energy model still applies, but your symptom patterns may differ significantly from someone not on HRT.
sexualHealth.disclaimer: This app is a planning tool, not medical advice. Always consult your provider for reproductive and sexual health decisions.

medications.disclaimer: Hormone therapy and other medications significantly affect energy, sleep, and symptom patterns. Phase-based guidance should be adapted accordingly. Always follow your provider's advice.

ui.safetyDisclaimer: This is a planning dashboard, not a diagnostic tool. Nothing here is medical advice. Discuss all health decisions with your provider.
